question: Are the firmware version/build strings at fixed addresses usable as a runtime identity guard?
callsite_evidence: The exact 3.101.036 IDB and firmware image contain 3.101.036 at 0x0C0C0810 and CONBINE_LTALM078_T3.101.036_06242053 at 0x0C0C0850.
The previous target metadata value ending in 06011854 was disproven on device when the module loaded but its constructor identity guard returned before /dev/canopus registration.
control_flow_evidence: The supervisor constructor compares both fixed-address strings before supervisor initialization and register_driver.
The corrected 3.101.036 supervisor embeds 06242053 and passes the exact-target ELF verifier.
ownership_analysis: read-only firmware strings; borrowed for module lifetime
unsafe_assumptions: string comparison is not a full SHA-256 recompute; complete SHA remains the offline release constraint
recommended_probe: minimal fixed-address read of both strings in the module constructor
